title: Single-cell decoding of breast cancer organotropism: ecosystem mapping for precision therapy
task: Map organotropic vulnerabilities in breast cancer metastasis across organs
key_results: Identified organ-specific programs: RARRES2-PTEN-mTOR in brain, DLAT-fatty acid oxidation in lung, TDO2+ fibroblast-mediated ferroptosis resistance in lung, IL-34-CSF1R-ARG1+ macrophage immunosuppression in brain, MAF-CD248 dormancy in bone
comments: Ambitious synthesis of multi-omic data proposing therapeutic strategies, though translation from organoid/spatial maps to clinical efficacy remains validation-limited.

model_io.model: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics of metastatic lesions

hypotheses.hypothesis: Conserved programs (hypoxic memory, stemness, immune evasion) operate alongside organ-specific adaptations in metastatic colonization
hypotheses.result: Confirmed by multi-omic profiling revealing organ-selective metabolic and immunological rewiring

hypotheses.hypothesis: Targeting niche-directed factors rather than tumor cytotoxicity will improve metastasis interception
hypotheses.result: Framework proposed but clinical validation outstanding

title: The RBMS1–SLC7A11 axis regulates ferroptosis susceptibility and lenvatinib sensitivity in hepatocellular carcinoma
task: Elucidate the RBMS1–SLC7A11 axis in regulating ferroptosis susceptibility and lenvatinib sensitivity in hepatocellular carcinoma
key_results: RBMS1 post-transcriptionally upregulates SLC7A11 to suppress ferroptosis and lenvatinib sensitivity; RBMS1 knockdown synergizes with lenvatinib by sensitizing cells to ferroptotic oxidative damage; xenograft studies confirm in vivo synergy
comments: Well-designed epistatic and xenograft validation establishes causal mechanistic connection, though broader applicability to other tyrosine kinase inhibitor-ferroptosis interactions remains unaddressed.

model_io.model: Cell culture system (HepG2, Huh7 hepatocellular carcinoma cells)
Transcriptomic profiling and clinical tissue analysis

hypotheses.hypothesis: RBMS1 acts as a post-transcriptional regulator of SLC7A11 to suppress ferroptosis
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: RBMS1 overexpression increases SLC7A11 protein, neutralizes ROS, and blocks lipid peroxidation; RBMS1 knockdown reverses this

hypotheses.hypothesis: SLC7A11 is epistatic to RBMS1 in mediating drug tolerance and ferroptosis evasion
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: SLC7A11 knockdown abrogates the protective and lenvatinib-resistance phenotypes conferred by RBMS1 hyperactivation

hypotheses.hypothesis: RBMS1 depletion sensitizes xenografts to lenvatinib therapy in vivo
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: RBMS1 knockdown significantly potentiates lenvatinib antitumor efficacy

title: The SPATA5-SPATA5L1-CINP-C1ORF109 complex is essential for cytoplasmic pre-60S ribosome maturation

key_results: SPATA5–SPATA5L1–CINP–C1ORF109 (55LCC) complex is essential for metazoan pre-60S maturation; SPATA5 ATPase activity is rate-limiting; complex evolved from yeast Drg1 monomer into multiprotein assembly
comments: Structural and functional characterization is solid, though the physiological consequences of 55LCC dysfunction in vivo remain to be explored.

model_io.model: Protein-protein interaction screen of endogenously tagged ribosome biogenesis factors

hypotheses.hypothesis: All four 55LCC subunits are essential for cytoplasmic pre-60S maturation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed by acute depletion showing maturation block

hypotheses.result: Confirmed by mutational analysis pinpointing SPATA5 as rate-limiting

title: Evaluation of redox dynamics in callus-forming skeletal progenitor cells during fracture healing using in vivo DNP-MRI
task: Visualize redox dynamics in callus-forming skeletal progenitor cells during fracture healing

title: RobustCell: a model attack-defense framework for robust transcriptomic data analysis

comments: ODE model captures clinical spectrum of refractoriness, but lacks validation in formally classified difficult-to-treat patients; molecular plausibility without clinical proof-of-concept remains a limitation.
